questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to detect fixed bit patterns with pure bitwise ops, no loops or conditionals, reinforcing shifts, masking, and truthiness evaluation.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts align neighboring bits
- Combining with AND tests multiple bit conditions simultaneously
- Pure bitwise approach scales to fixed-width inputs without branching

## Code Example
```c
bool hasPattern101(uint32_t n) {
  return (n & (n >> 2) & ~(n >> 1)) != 0;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for 64-bit inputs?
- What edge cases exist near the topmost bits (i=29) and how does masking affect them?

## Why This Is Asked

This tests precise bit-twiddling with non-trivial masks and no loops, a common optimization pattern.

## Key Concepts

- Mask construction for adjacent-bit swaps
- Two-shift strategy and one return
- Edge cases: 64-bit boundaries, unsigned masking

## Code Example

```c
uint64_t swapAdjacent64(uint64_t n) {
  const uint64_t E = 0x5555555555555555ULL;
  const uint64_t O = 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAULL;
  return ((n & E) << 1) | ((n & O) >> 1);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you generalize to swap every 3-bit group? 
- What are the performance implications on modern CPUs?
